verdict.rationale: Simular documents a BYOD mode: users can download Sai and run it on their own Mac or Windows device, and it publishes an open-source computer-control agent framework. Neither clearly amounts to self-hosting the core Sai service, because the evidence does not show the backend, planning or API running on user infrastructure. The open-source framework is not shown to be the Sai product itself. Missing for 10: documented self-hosted deployment of the Sai backend/API, clarity that BYOD runs without Simular's cloud, evidence that the open-source framework is the core product, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: Users can download Sai to get it running on their own device environment with control and privacy.
Sai does it on a cloud computer or your own device
An open-source framework for agents that control computers like a human — UI, keyboard, and mouse — across environments.
